question.worked_solution:
Notice that the logarithms share the same base.

First, we apply the power rule to the *first* term to make the coefficient in front of each logarithm the same:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{log}_{6}⁡(3x)-{log}_{6}⁡(2{x}^{2}+1) & ={log}_{6}⁡3 \\ {log}_{6}⁡(9{x}^{2})-{log}_{6}⁡(2{x}^{2}+1) & ={log}_{6}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we combine the logarithms on the left-hand side using the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{6}⁡(\frac{9{x}^{2}}{2{x}^{2}+1}) & ={log}_{6}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the equation for $x$ using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9{x}^{2}}{2{x}^{2}+1} & =3 \\ (2{x}^{2}+1)\cdot \frac{9{x}^{2}}{2{x}^{2}+1} & =(2{x}^{2}+1)\cdot 3 \\ \cancel{(2{x}^{2}+1)}\cdot \frac{9{x}^{2}}{\cancel{2{x}^{2}+1}} & =(2{x}^{2}+1)\cdot 3 \\ 9{x}^{2} & =6{x}^{2}+3 \\ 3{x}^{2} & =3 \\ {x}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=-1$ or $x=1.$ 

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=-1$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{log}_{6}⁡(3\cdot (-1))-{log}_{6}⁡(2(-1)^{2}+1) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{6}⁡3 \\ 2{log}_{6}⁡(-3)-{log}_{6}⁡(3) & \ne {log}_{6}⁡3\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

because ${log}_{6}⁡(-3)$ is undefined. Therefore, $x=-1$ is not a valid solution.

- Substituting $x=1$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{log}_{6}⁡(3\cdot 1)-{log}_{6}⁡(2(1)^{2}+1) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{6}⁡3 \\ 2{log}_{6}⁡3-{log}_{6}⁡3 & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{6}⁡3 \\ (2-1){log}_{6}⁡3 & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{6}⁡3 \\ {log}_{6}⁡3 & ={log}_{6}⁡3\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=1$ is a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$x=1$ only".
